Quarto renders LaTeX math via KaTeX and has built-in theorem environments.

::: {#thm-euclid}
## Euclid
There are infinitely many primes.
:::

::: {.proof}
Suppose $p_1, \dots, p_n$ are all the primes and let
$N = p_1 p_2 \cdots p_n + 1$. Any prime factor of $N$ differs from
every $p_i$, a contradiction.
:::

As @thm-euclid shows, the primes never run out. A display equation:

$$
\zeta(s) = \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n^s} = \prod_{p} \frac{1}{1-p^{-s}}, \qquad \operatorname{Re}(s) > 1.
$$ {#eq-euler}

Code blocks are syntax-highlighted (this one is shown, not executed):

```python
def sieve(n):
    is_prime = [True] * (n + 1)
    is_prime[0:2] = [False, False]
    for i in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1):
        if is_prime[i]:
            is_prime[i*i::i] = [False] * len(is_prime[i*i::i])
    return [i for i, p in enumerate(is_prime) if p]
```
